items.title: File Alameda County business personal property return
items.description: California business property statements (Form 571-L) are due April 1 and a 10% penalty applies if not filed by May 7. This is the Business Property Statement; businesses with $100,000 or more of taxable property must file even without a request.

items.title: File the Alameda County transient occupancy tax return
items.description: Applies to hotels, motels and short-term rentals in the unincorporated area. The monthly remittance form is due the last day of the following month, mailed to the Business License Tax Unit in Hayward (form uploaded 2023; confirm the current version and rate).

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File Kern County business personal property return
items.description: California businesses whose taxable business property cost $100,000 or more on January 1 (or that the assessor asks) file the Business Property Statement (Form BOE-571-L) with the county assessor by April 1 (next business day if a weekend or holiday); a late or missing statement means an estimated value plus a 10% penalty (Revenue and Taxation Code 463). The county's own assessor page was not individually confirmed; the state rule applies. The link is the state Board of Equalization property tax forms page.

note: Unincorporated Kern County requires a transient occupancy tax certificate for each rental unit (a third-party guide says 6%), but no official due date was found.

items.title: File Los Angeles County business personal property return
items.description: California business property statements (Form 571-L) are due April 1 and a 10% penalty applies if not filed by May 7. This is the Business Property Statement; businesses with $100,000 or more of taxable property must file even without a request.

items.title: File the Los Angeles County transient occupancy tax return
items.authority: Los Angeles County Treasurer and Tax Collector
items.description: Applies to hotels, motels and short-term rentals in the unincorporated area. The tax is 12% of rent, including home-sharing rentals, due on or before the last day of the month after the reporting month (County Code title 4, chapter 4.72). Late payment costs 10% within a month and 20% after, plus 1.5% monthly interest.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File the Marin County transient occupancy tax return
items.description: Applies to hotels, motels and short-term rentals in the unincorporated area. The rate is 10%, or 14% in West Marin. Returns are due by close of business on the last day of the month for the prior month; 10% penalty up to 30 days late and a second 10% after, plus 0.5% monthly interest.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File the Orange County transient occupancy tax return
items.description: Applies to hotels, motels and short-term rentals in the unincorporated area. The tax is 10% of rent. Returns are quarterly; the instructions say payment is due by the last business day of the month after the quarter (the program page says within one calendar month). A return is required even if no tax is due; a late return costs 10% plus 1.5% interest.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File Placer County business personal property return
items.description: California business property statements (Form 571-L) are due April 1 and a 10% penalty applies if not filed by May 7. This is the Business Property Statement; businesses with $100,000 or more of taxable property must file even without a request.

items.title: File the Placer County transient occupancy tax return
items.description: Applies to hotels, motels and short-term rentals in the unincorporated area. Returns are quarterly, due on or before the last day of the month after each quarter (a county table lists the 1st as due and the month's end as the delinquency date); operators collecting more than $400,000 in a fiscal year file monthly the next year. A return is required even with no rentals.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File the Riverside County transient occupancy tax return
items.description: Applies to hotels, motels and short-term rentals in the unincorporated area. The tax is 10% of gross rent including mandatory fees. The quarterly return is due the last day of the month after each quarter and is required even if no tax is due; stays over 30 days need the exemption form with the return. Airbnb remits for bookings made through it.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental

items.title: File the Sacramento County transient occupancy tax return
items.description: Applies to hotels, motels and short-term rentals in the unincorporated area. The return form says the tax is due by the last day of the month after collection and must be filed even when no tax is owed. It shows a 12% rate and a 10% penalty (20% after 30 days) plus 1.5% monthly interest; the form is undated, so confirm the current rate.

appliesWhen.description: Operates a hotel, motel or short-term rental
